rationale: The two verses share the noun ruach in the same 'haughty/lowly of spirit' slot: רֽוּחַ (oshb:Prov.16.18, 'height of spirit') and ר֭וּחַ (oshb:Prov.16.19, 'lowly of spirit'), and they share the pride root as well: גָּא֑וֹן (oshb:Prov.16.18, 'pride') and גֵּאִֽים (oshb:Prov.16.19, 'the proud'). Two shared roots in consecutive verses turn the famous pride-before-a-fall line and the lowly-spirit saying that follows it into a bound pair. The inventory records a ketiv/qere note at Prov.16.19: an inline ketiv עניים precedes the qere עֲנָוִ֑ים.
rejected_alternative: Keeping 16:18 as its own well-known proverb was the initial draft; the pairing was adopted once both the ruach and the ge'ah/ga'on root were confirmed shared with 16:19 rather than assumed from familiarity with the verse alone.

The x-small nun (other_segs, single-witness) sits inside this span at Prov.16.28, a scribal seg disclosed here as texture, not as boundary evidence. Prov.16.27 also carries a ketiv/qere note on the word for 'lips', disclosed for completeness though it plays no role in the ish-opening evidence that drives this row.
